title: Hajime_Botnet_Investigation_b78
description: Investigate and identify malicious activity in the network, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and identify any malicious activity related to the Hajime botnet family, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the victim host `victim` with the username `ubuntu` and password `ubuntu`. From there, you can investigate the network and connected devices. Enter the word `start` to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the victim host `victim` with the username `ubuntu` and password `ubuntu`. From there, you can investigate the network and connected devices. Enter the word `start` to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication. The correct answer is the service name `bot-beacon.service`.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, start by listing all systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for any unusual or recently created services. The service name you are looking for is `bot-beacon.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Start by understanding the systemd services and how they are managed. Look for any services that seem out of place or recently created.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. This will help you identify any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service you are looking for is named `bot-beacon.service`. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service | grep bot-beacon.service` to find it.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic. The correct answer is the service name `bot-flood.service`.
levels.solution: To identify the abnormal traffic service, list all systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for services that are not standard system services and check their configuration files. The service name you are looking for is `bot-flood.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Focus on services that are not standard system services. These might be responsible for generating abnormal network traffic.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. Then, inspect the configuration files of any suspicious services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service you are looking for is named `bot-flood.service`. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service | grep bot-flood.service` to find it.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. The correct answer is the timer name `system-update-checker.timer`.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, investigate the systemd timers and services. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. Look for any timers that are scheduled to run the suspicious services. The timer name you are looking for is `system-update-checker.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Understand how systemd timers and services work together to schedule tasks. Look for timers that might be responsible for starting the suspicious services.

hints.title: Command Suggestions
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. This will help you identify any timers that are scheduled to run the suspicious services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The timer you are looking for is named `system-update-checker.timer`. Use the command `systemctl list-timers | grep system-update-checker.timer` to find it.
